Boiser, reboiser.

examples.text: Um die Gefahr von Erdrutschen zu bannen, werden Versuche unternommen, die kahlen Hänge zu bewalden.
examples.translation: Afin d’éviter le danger de glissements de terrain, des tentatives sont faites pour boiser les pentes dénudées.

glosses: mit vielen Bäumen (Wald) bepflanzen

examples.text: „Nun fängt man dort wieder an, die dürren Höhen zu bewalden, denn Erfahrung hat Lehre gebracht. Aber wer wird einst unsere Gebirge wieder bewalden können und wollen?!“

glosses: als Wald langsam aber sicher eine größere Fläche einnehmen und ehemals freies Gelände zu Wald werden lassen

examples.text: „Die größere Trockenheit des Klimas in der postglacialen Zeit wie die zunehmende Entfernung des wasserspendenden Gletschers ließ allmählich die Wasserläufe zu geringerer Breite zusammenschwinden, die Steppen bewaldeten sich.“

glosses: To cover an area with trees.

examples.text: From the view-point of national economy professor Fehér communicates to us most interesting facts, which he has established in an important question now of actuality : in the subject of foresting the Great Hungarian Plains.

glosses: A dense uncultivated tract of trees and undergrowth, larger than woods.

examples.text: Who after Archimagoes fowle defeat / Led her away into a foreſt wilde, / And turning wrathfull fyre to luſtfull heat, / With beaſtly ſin though her to haue defilde, / And made the vaſſal of his pleaſures vilde.

Since the mid-1980s, when Indonesia first began to clear its bountiful forests on an industrial scale in favour of lucrative palm-oil plantations, “haze” has become an almost annual occurrence in South-East Asia. The cheapest way to clear logged woodland is to burn it, producing an acrid cloud of foul white smoke that, carried by the wind, can cover hundreds, or even thousands, of square miles.

glosses: Any dense collection or amount.

examples.text: a forest of criticism
Squealing and still propelled by the kick, the calf scrabbled through the forest of legs and into the open.

glosses: A defined area of land set aside in England as royal hunting ground or for other privileged use; all such areas.

examples.text: Throughout the 1500s, the populace roiled over a constellation of grievances of which the forest emerged as a key focal point. The popular late Middle Ages fictional character Robin Hood, dressed in green to symbolize the forest, dodged fines for forest offenses and stole from the rich to give to the poor. But his appeal was painfully real and embodied the struggle over wood.
[…] in places such as the Forest of Bowland there is hardly a tree in sight and much of the area is a vast tract of almost barren gritstone hills and peat moorland.

glosses: A graph with no cycles; i.e., a graph made up of trees.

examples.text: Let H be a traversal of an undirected graph G = (X, U). For given H, the set U can be split into set of tree edges from the forest G_H and the set of inverse edges that do not belong to this forest.

glosses: A group of domains that are managed as a unit.

examples.text: Forests are considered the security boundary in Active Directory; by this we mean that if you need to definitively restrict access to a resource within a particular domain so that administrators from other domains do not have any access to it whatsoever, you need to implement a separate forest instead of using an additional domain within the current forest.

glosses: The color forest green.
Garnir de menuiserie.

examples.text: Elle est boisée tout autour, la boisure de la fenêtre est ornée d’une sculpture dorée.

glosses: Garnir de bois ; planter d’arbres.

examples.text: […] cependant, la pinède sur lande provoque une accélération de l’évolution podzolique, conduisant la lande sur podzol […] ; celle-ci est particulièrement difficile à boiser, et se comporte comme un groupement stable : c’est la lande paraclimacique.

glosses: Rater la frappe d’une balle (sur le cadre de la raquette).
